name: Linux Forensic Artifacts
description: Extraction and analysis of Linux-specific forensic artifacts. Covers systemd journal and syslog analysis, authentication logs (auth.log, secure, wtmp, btmp, lastlog), shell history files, cron and systemd timer/service persistence, package manager logs (dpkg, apt, yum/dnf), SSH artifacts (authorized_keys, known_hosts), auditd logs, user and service account configuration, and ext4/XFS-specific timestamp and journal behaviour. Windows artifacts are covered by DFIR-DISK-ARTIFACTS and macOS artifacts by DFIR-DISK-MACART.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to Linux forensic artifact analysis

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands Linux artifact categories and their forensic value
evidence: Can describe major Linux artifact sources (journald, syslog, auth logs, shell history, cron)
Understands how distribution differences affect log locations and formats
Can explain the forensic implications of ext4 and XFS timestamps, including crtime support

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Extracts and parses Linux artifacts under supervision
evidence: Parsed systemd journals offline from a disk image using journalctl --directory or equivalent under guidance
Extracted login history from wtmp, btmp, and auth.log/secure with supervisor review
Reviewed shell history, cron tables, and systemd unit files for evidence of attacker activity
Parsed package manager logs to identify installed or removed software

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently analyses Linux artifacts across investigation types
evidence: Independently analysed Linux artifacts in 5+ investigations across multiple distributions
Correlates journal, auth log, shell history, and filesystem timestamps to reconstruct attacker activity
Identifies persistence via cron, systemd services and timers, SSH keys, shell profiles, and LD_PRELOAD
Produces Linux forensic reports withstanding peer and legal review

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Handles advanced Linux forensic scenarios; detects anti-forensics
evidence: Identifies evidence of Linux anti-forensics (log truncation, history disabling, timestomping, journal tampering)
Recovers deleted log and history content from ext4 journals or unallocated space
Develops custom parsers for Linux artifacts from new distributions or application stacks
Reviews and mentors junior examiners on Linux artifact analysis

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Authority on Linux forensics; discovers new artifact sources
evidence: Authored or maintains lab's Linux forensic analysis procedures
Published research on Linux artifacts or analysis techniques
Validated forensic tool accuracy against Linux ground truth data
Provides expert testimony on Linux forensic evidence

assessment_methods.description: Given a Linux server disk image from a simulated intrusion, extract and analyse platform-specific artifacts to establish initial access, attacker commands, and persistence within a specified timeframe
Review Linux artifact analysis sections from recent case reports
